Have you ever zoned out on a Zoom call, then realised you’ve missed the last two minutes? I’ve been trying Wispr Flow’s Notetaker, which records and transcribes meetings in real time. You can ask it what you missed, search previous meetings for specific decisions, and use the transcripts with tools like ChatGPT and Claude to draft follow-up emails or messages. Very useful if, like me, you spend a lot of time in meetings, and even more time trying to remember what actually happened in them.  It’s currently available on Mac and Windows, and the Notetaker is free to use. Copy the link for one month of Wispr Flow Pro for free: https://ref.wisprflow.ai/ali_tiktok_notetaker

If you're struggling to figure out what to do with your life, try the Odyssey Plan. It's an exercise that Stanford Business School uses to help people figure out their path. You ask yourself three questions: 1️⃣ Your current path: If you continued down your current path, what would your life look like 5 years from now? 2️⃣ Your alternative path: If you had to take a completely different path, what would your life look like 5 years from now? 3️⃣ Your radical path: If you took a completely different path but didn't care what anyone thought and weren't worried about money, what would your life look like? A UTI can become much more than a urinary problem for older women. On unPAUSED, we discuss how these infections can become serious and potentially lead to sepsis. We also explore a possible connection between infection-related confusion, falls, and hip fractures. A woman who becomes confused, tries to get out of bed to use the bathroom, and falls may be facing more than one health crisis at once. It’s a conversation that shows why urinary health deserves more attention as women age. ✨Listen to the full conversation at the link in my bio.  #uti #womenshealth #menopause #hormonehealth #healthcare

Using “warming” lube? More ingredients don’t necessarily mean a better experience. On this episode of unPAUSED I dive into everything you need to know about GSM, and answer your most asked questions. Including why peppermint oil, fragrance, and unnecessary extras can make discomfort worse, especially when vaginal tissue is already irritated. The takeaway here: keep it simple. Look for fragrance-free products with as few ingredients as possible. You don’t need all the bells and whistles in your lubricant. ✨Listen to the full episode at the link in bio.  #menopause #gsm #vaginalhealth #midlife #womenshealth

I’ve been a physician for decades, and this one surprised me. Dense breasts don’t just make cancer harder to spot on a mammogram. They also raise your risk of breast cancer. About half of women have dense breasts, and many don’t know what that means for their screening. This week on unPAUSED, breast oncologist, Eleonora Teplinsky, MD breaks down when to ask your doctor about an MRI or ultrasound. ✨Listen to the full episode at the link in bio.  #breastcancer #breastcancerawareness #breastcancersupport  #womenshealth #healthcare

The menopause guideline most OB-GYNs have practiced under was written in 2014, before the newest nonhormonal drugs existed and before the FDA changed the hormone therapy label. On October 15, ACOG replaced it: Clinical Practice Guideline No. 13, published in Obstetrics & Gynecology (2026), covering hot flushes, sleep, and mood. Hormone therapy is strongly recommended for hot flushes and the sleep disruption they cause, started before 60 or within 10 years of menopause; continuing past 60 may be necessary if symptoms persist.
